name: Familial Intraosseous Vascular Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Familial Intraosseous Vascular Malformation Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of at least one first-degree relative with confirmed intraosseous vascular malformation
Imaging demonstrating characteristic intraosseous vascular lesions with radiolucent, honeycomb or soap-bubble appearance
Biopsy confirming vascular malformation within bone tissue without evidence of malignancy
Presence of localized bone swelling or deformity consistent with vascular malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of family history plus radiologic evidence of intraosseous vascular malformation; histopathology supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but no specific gene identified yet

pathognomonic.notes: Radiologically visible vascular malformation within bone
searchTerms: localized blood vessel lesion in bone

pathognomonic.symptomName: Familial clustering of intraosseous vascular malformations
searchTerms: family history of bone vascular malformations

common.notes: Often painless but visible or palpable

common.symptomName: Intermittent bone pain at lesion site
searchTerms: bone discomfort that comes and goes
bone lesions appearing dark on X-ray
areas of bone loss on imaging

common.symptomName: Mild functional impairment of affected bone
common.notes: Depending on lesion size and location

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue swelling adjacent to bone lesion
searchTerms: soft tissue swelling near bone lesion

occasional.symptomName: Mild localized warmth or erythema over lesion
searchTerms: localized warmth or redness over lesion
mild skin inflammation near bone lesion

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to lesion compression
rare.notes: If lesion located near neural structures
searchTerms: symptoms caused by lesion pressing on nerves

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large vascular malformations
searchTerms: heart failure from large vascular malformations
heart failure due to vascular lesions

laboratory: Typically normal blood counts and inflammatory markers
imaging: X-ray showing radiolucent, honeycomb or soap-bubble intraosseous lesions
MRI demonstrating vascular channels within bone
CT scan delineating extent of bone involvement
genetic: Familial inheritance pattern observed; specific gene mutations not yet identified
other: Histopathology revealing dilated vascular channels within bone trabeculae without malignancy

distinguishingFeatures: Cutaneous or soft tissue vascular malformations present

redFlags: Severe localized pain unresponsive to analgesics
references: Schwartz HS, et al. Intraosseous vascular malformations: clinical and radiologic features. Skeletal Radiol. 2015.
Mulliken JB, Glowacki J. Hemangiomas and vascular malformations in infants and children: a classification based on endothelial characteristics. Plast Reconstr Surg. 1982.
